generatedCommentsNodes.comment:
The method names `StYMax.fromWellKnownBinaryGeo(value)` and `StYMin.fromWellKnownBinaryGeo(value)` suggest that these methods are specific to Geo WKB data. However, the class names `StYMaxFromWKB` and `StYMinFromWKB` do not reflect this specificity. It would be more consistent if the class names were also updated to reflect the Geo aspect, such as `StYMaxFromWKBGeo` and `StYMinFromWKBGeo`.
The `evalValue` method is duplicated in each of these classes. This duplication can be avoided by creating a common superclass or utility class that contains this method. This would reduce code redundancy and improve maintainability.

The `fromWellKnownBinary` and `fromWellKnownBinaryGeo` methods in all four classes (`StEnvelope`, `StXMax`, `StXMin`, `StYMax`) have a common issue. When the geometry is a `Point`, they return the WKB of the point instead of the required coordinate value (envelope or x/y). This will lead to incorrect results.
The `fromWellKnownBinary` and `fromWellKnownBinaryGeo` methods in all four classes do not handle the case where `geometry instanceof Point` correctly. For `StXMax`, `StXMin`, and `StYMax`, these methods should return the x or y coordinate of the point, respectively. For `StEnvelope`, it should throw an exception since a single point does not have an envelope.
In the `resolveType` method of `StEnvelope`, if the field's data type is neither `GEO_POINT`, `GEO_SHAPE`, `CARTESIAN_POINT`, nor `CARTESIAN_SHAPE`, it sets the `dataType` to `NULL`. This might not be the intended behavior. Typically, such a case would result in an error or a different handling mechanism.
The `resolveType` method in `StXMax`, `StXMin`, and `StYMax` does not set any internal state based on the resolved type. This is consistent with their design since they always return a `DOUBLE`. However, it's worth noting that these methods do not provide feedback if the input type is invalid beyond returning an error in the evaluator.

The method names `evalValue` are duplicated across multiple classes (`StXMaxFromWKBGeoEvaluator`, `StXMinFromWKBEvaluator`, `StXMinFromWKBGeoEvaluator`, `StYMaxFromWKBEvaluator`). This duplication can lead to maintenance issues. Consider refactoring the common logic into a shared utility class or method.
The `evalValue` methods in each class call different static methods (`StXMax.fromWellKnownBinaryGeo`, `StXMin.fromWellKnownBinary`, `StXMin.fromWellKnownBinaryGeo`, `StYMax.fromWellKnownBinary`). This inconsistency can lead to confusion and errors. Ensure that the correct method is called based on the evaluator's purpose.
The `evalBlock` methods in each class handle multiple values per position by checking if `valueCount > 1`. However, the logic for handling multiple values is identical across all classes. Consider refactoring this common logic into a shared method to improve maintainability.
The `BytesRef scratchPad` is created in each method (`evalVector`, `evalBlock`) where it is used. This can be optimized by reusing the `scratchPad` if possible, to reduce object creation overhead.

The class names `StEnvelopeFromWKBEvaluator`, `StEnvelopeFromWKBGeoEvaluator`, and `StXMaxFromWKBEvaluator` suggest they are handling WKB (Well-Known Binary) data. However, the methods `fromWellKnownBinary` and `fromWellKnownBinaryGeo` imply different processing for WKB and Geo formats. The class names should reflect this distinction more clearly to avoid confusion.
Both `StEnvelopeFromWKBEvaluator` and `StEnvelopeFromWKBGeoEvaluator` have nearly identical code except for the method call in `evalValue`. This duplication can be refactored into a common superclass or utility class to reduce redundancy and improve maintainability.
In `StXMaxFromWKBEvaluator`, the `evalBlock` method uses a `DoubleBlock.Builder` which is appropriate for returning double values. However, similar to the other evaluators, consider refactoring common logic into a superclass or utility class to avoid code duplication.

+// end::st_envelope-result[]
+;
+
+polygonEnvelopeXYMinMax
+required_capability: st_envelope

review_comment: While mathematically correct, I find this more confusing than it should be, since you're comparing both min and maxes with both min and maxes :)
There's a lot of copy paste between all 4 X/Y Min/Max tests. Although this is test code, it could easily be refactored out using an abstract test template.

I looked through the differences between two tests and the the number of lines that are actually the same is quite low. Mostly they are very similar, but not identical. I think any effort to reduce duplication will add complexity and make the tests harder to follow.
This 4x copy paste with 2 line differences could easily be factored out, and the JIT should take care of any performance issues.

I thought about common code, where we pass in functions for the two unique calls (eg. getY and getYMax), but that creates much harder to read code, and saves only a few lines of code duplication, so I thought it was not worth it.

review_comment: This class is in lib/geo because it is needed by both `ESQL` for the `ST_ENVELOPE` function as well as in the compute engine for the `ST_EXTENT` aggregation. It seems generic enough for libs/geo, but another choice would be to put it in the compute engine. I did not do that because there was no obvious place for generic spatial utils there. We could make one, of course.
I think this implementation might evolve quite a bit so let's leave it here for now
To allow this to be used outside of this class, consider extracting this to a static method, maybe in another `class`.

These should be either be `protected` or exposed via getters so they can be used by its clients, e.g., during intermediate serialization. For my money, I prefer getters, due to the whole "prefer composition to inheritance".
Got this from the changes in ST_EXTENT PR.
Since this can return `null`, it should return `Optional<Rectangle>` (Or at the very least be marked with `@Nullable`, but `Optional` is better)
It should never return null. I removed the one case where it does.
